statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of the home listing, a representative result-chart detail page, terms, and a real 404 recovery state.

page.framework: server-rendered HTML with third-party Google consent/ads and Firebase notification scripts
page.notes: Public, mobile-first, time-sensitive result publication. Home and detail templates are very long tables; a consent wall appears on fresh visits.

paths.description: Homepage/current-results listing: primary content template, monthly chart selector, consent entry state, responsive/preferences/performance/security evidence. Represents the repeated result-list sections.
Delhi Dream record-chart page: representative detail/history archetype reached through a Record Chart link; other game chart URLs share this template and were de-duplicated.
Terms of Service: representative legal/content page linked from the disclaimer.
Real unknown route: representative HTTP 404 and recovery state.

findings.summary: The site has no dark color scheme.
findings.evidence: Dark-mode screenshot is pixel-equivalent to the light capture; DOM reports color-scheme: normal and the light #f1f1f1 page background remains.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define semantic surface/text tokens with light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme fallback.

findings.summary: A blinking animation continues under reduced-motion preference.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched prefers-reduced-motion: reduce but still found blink-animation running with a 1500 ms duration.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable the blink animation in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), leaving a static state indicator.

findings.summary: Navigation between the results list and chart pages swaps abruptly.
findings.evidence: The motion probe found no view-transition meta/CSS; the representative Record Chart journey performs a full cross-document navigation with no continuity cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Opt matching same-origin pages into cross-document View Transitions under prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and give persistent elements stable transition names.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures the primary content on every fresh visit.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile load screenshots show a modal and dimmed backdrop covering the first viewport before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface where lawful, add an equally prominent reject action, preserve access to essential content, and use a native dialog with predictable dismissal when modality is necessary.

findings.summary: Most chart links are too small for reliable touch use.
findings.evidence: The modality probe found 118 of 128 visible interactive targets below 24 px in at least one dimension; repeated Record Chart links are about 76x15 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase each result-row link hit area to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44, and add an explicit high-contrast :focus-visible style.

findings.summary: The 404 state explains the failure but offers no recovery action.
findings.evidence: The real 404 screenshot and probe show Page Not Found, but zero links and zero buttons, so users cannot return home or search from the error state.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a real link to the homepage and a useful route back to current results; preserve the 404 HTTP status.

findings.summary: Lab LCP is slow despite a light first-party document.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.3 s, FCP 2.4 s, TTI 6.6 s, and a performance score of 72. The direct trace was faster, so confidence is medium and the throttled Lighthouse result identifies a network-sensitive load path.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize above-fold content, defer nonessential consent/ad/notification work, and remove font and third-party dependency contention from the critical path.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts dominate transfer and the critical dependency graph.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 736,901 transferred bytes; 666,535 bytes across 19 requests were third-party. Ads, Tag Manager and Funding Choices account for most bytes, while Lighthouse reports a 1.5 s longest dependency chain.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate advertising and analytics until consent, remove unused notification/ads dependencies, self-host only the font weights used, and keep third-party code off the critical rendering path.

findings.summary: The chart form and data tables lack essential accessible semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse flags both month/year selects without labels, two fake table captions, and data cells without associated headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate visible labels with both selects, use caption elements, and mark table headers with th plus scope or headers/id associations.

findings.summary: Multiple core text colors fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured ratios including 1.53:1 for the disclaimer link, 2.05:1 for the main results heading, 2.82:1 for status headings, and 3.05:1 for chart links on yellow.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace decorative palette values with tested semantic color pairs meeting 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text/UI.

findings.summary: The long document lacks a coherent landmark and heading hierarchy.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no main, nav, header or footer elements and many H1 elements, including consent-vendor headings injected into the page structure.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the primary results in main, use one page H1 with ordered section headings, add a skip link, and keep third-party modal headings isolated from document hierarchy.

findings.summary: The primary results are extremely dense and use very small repeated labels.
findings.evidence: The mobile page is about 9,050 px tall; repeated chart links render around 12.8 px text in 15 px-high boxes, making scanning and comprehension difficult.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase body/link type and line height, group results into navigable sections, and use disclosure or filtering without hiding crawlable content.

findings.summary: Both page images omit intrinsic dimensions.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found two of two images without width and height attributes. A small measured CLS of 0.05 corroborates some late movement, though it does not prove both images caused it.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width and height attributes matching each SVG aspect ratio so the browser reserves space before load.

findings.summary: The page is excluded from the back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons, including Cache-Control: no-store on the main resource.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove no-store from public result pages unless it is strictly required; use revalidation directives that permit BFCache and verify return navigation.

findings.summary: Hundreds of links repeat the non-descriptive label “Record Chart”.
findings.evidence: The internal-link probe enumerated result URLs whose anchor text is repeatedly only Record Chart, making destination meaning weak out of context.
findings.suggestedFix: Include the game name in each link’s visible or accessible text, for example “Delhi Dream record chart”.

findings.summary: The public site has no sitemap at the advertised conventional location.
findings.evidence: An in-browser fetch returned 404 for /sitemap.xml while representative pages expose distinct canonical URLs and robots.txt returns 200.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish a sitemap containing canonical result/chart URLs and reference it from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Result pages have no structured data or social preview metadata.
findings.evidence: Home and detail metadata probes found zero JSON-LD blocks and no Open Graph tags, despite the pages representing time-sensitive result datasets.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate WebSite/Dataset or other appropriate schema.org JSON-LD and Open Graph title, description, URL and image metadata that match visible content.

findings.summary: Security headers are absent and site cookies are not marked Secure.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy headers. All three observed first-party cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None; analytics cookies last 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy CSP in report-only then enforced mode, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a minimal Permissions-Policy; mark HTTPS cookies Secure and choose Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is required.

findings.summary: The privacy and tracking footprint is disproportionate to the core text service.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 8 third-party origins and 3 known trackers. HAR attributes 90% of transfer bytes to third parties, while the consent UI describes processing with 210 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors, default nonessential processing off, delay tags until an affirmative choice, shorten analytics retention, and document each processor’s necessity.

findings.summary: Failure recovery dead-ends on the site’s 404 template.
findings.evidence: The tested 404 route returns an explanatory page but has no retry, home link, search, or current-results action.
findings.suggestedFix: Give error templates resilient navigation and retry affordances, and apply the same pattern to network/timeout states.

findings.summary: The layout is not prepared for other writing directions.
findings.evidence: The page correctly declares lang=en, but the style probe found 64 physical left/right declarations and zero logical-property rules; dir is not declared.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an explicit direction where appropriate and replace physical spacing/position properties with inline/block logical properties.

findings.summary: Result dates are rendered as fixed English strings rather than locale-aware data.
findings.evidence: Home and detail headings hard-code English month/day ordering across repeated result dates; no locale switch or locale-aware rendering signal was found. The underlying time element does include a machine-readable offset.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep machine-readable ISO values, format user-facing dates with Intl.DateTimeFormat for the selected locale, and separate content strings from templates.

findings.summary: Consent choices are asymmetric and the wall foregrounds acceptance.
findings.evidence: The first-layer modal offers Consent and Manage options but no equally prominent Reject all action; declining requires an additional path while content remains blocked.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide equally prominent accept and reject actions on the first layer, avoid preselected nonessential purposes, and keep withdrawal as easy as acceptance.

findings.summary: Third-party overhead is excessive for a mostly textual results page.
findings.evidence: The HAR shows 666,535 third-party bytes versus 70,366 first-party bytes, with ads, analytics, consent and notification libraries dominating the 737 KB load.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors, load nonessential scripts only after consent and idle, and avoid downloading notification code before user intent.

findings.summary: The in-memory footprint is high for a static result table.
findings.evidence: A single loaded state retained 317,209 heap nodes and 17,862,990 bytes self-size; third-party consent/ad code accounts for substantial native/code/closure populations. A separate post-scroll session measured 18.35 MB, but is not treated as proof of a leak.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary third-party runtimes, lazy-create consent detail UI, and profile retained objects after vendor/script reduction.

taskList.title: Minimize, consent-gate and defer third-party ads, analytics and notification code
Replace the blocking asymmetric consent wall with balanced, content-preserving choices
Fix text contrast, target sizing, labels, table semantics and landmarks
Deploy security headers and secure cookie attributes
Improve crawl/share metadata and descriptive links
Add useful recovery navigation to error templates
Prepare templates for locale and writing-direction variation
Restore BFCache eligibility and intrinsic image sizing
